_provenance.why: wq#4397 CONTRADICTed wq#4396 because mcp/server.py was written against an invented protocol ('op' key, exec/snapshot/send/logs command names) while the real daemon reads 'cmd' with the five names below. This file is the committed, immutable copy of that contract: tests assert the wrapper speaks only these commands, so the same class of drift fails a test instead of shipping 8/8 green with 0/4 tools working. tests/test_server.py::test_fixture_matches_real_remote_cli re-checks it against the live binary when one is present.

framing: one JSON object + newline per connection, one JSON object + newline back, then the daemon closes the connection
not_in_protocol: exec — remote-cli has no synchronous run-and-wait-for-exit-code command; the MCP `exec` tool is synthesized client-side from send_keys + polled scrollback
